subject: Transparent incident debrief and verification instructions
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@novabank.com>, NovaBank Engineering <eng+prod@novabank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Transparent incident debrief and verification instructions

Hi Sanjay / NovaBank team,

Thank you again for the time this morning. Attached is our consolidated debrief for the Apr 12 inference-serving disruption you experienced — the goal here is to be as transparent as possible and give you a clear path to verify the fixes on your side.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: KV-cache eviction race during a rare combined workload spike + a kernel-selection path that prevented an immediate fallback.
- Impact window: ~2027-04-12T03:22:00Z to 2027-04-12T03:47:00Z; elevated error rates and latency spikes for a subset of long-sequence, multi-turn calls.
- Customer-visible effects: ~0.6% of requests returned tokenization errors or stalled streams; requests were retried and recovered for most customers but we know this impacted some NovaBank workflows.

What we are sending you now:
1) RCA summary (PDF) — short narrative + technical appendix.
2) Event timeline (CSV) — per-shard traces and operator actions tied to timestamps.
3) Mitigation checklist (Excel) — the exact configuration changes we’ve applied and steps you can run to validate.

Immediate actions we’ve taken (completed):
- Disabled the kernel-selection fast-path that caused non-fallback behavior (hotfix v0.9.3 deployed at 2027-04-12T04:05:00Z).
- Tuned KV-cache eviction thresholds and added stronger telemetry to detect early eviction storms.
- Applied a quota throttle on high-seqlen continuous sessions to reduce burst surface area.

Planned/verifiable actions (next 30 days):
- Canary rollout of the reworked kernel-selection logic with A/B on dedicated pools (target: 2027-05-02).
- Post-deploy synthetic checks (we’ll share the test prompts and expected traces).
- Joint verification window: we propose a 48-hour verification starting 2027-04-25 where NovaBank runs representative traffic and we monitor together.

Quick ask: please confirm the best contact(s) for the joint verification window and whether 2027-04-25/26 works for you.

Attachments: 20270419_kv-drift_timeline.csv (CSV), 20270419_rca_summary.pdf (PDF), 20270419_mitigation-checklist.xlsx (XLSX)

Thanks — we want to make sure you have everything required to independently validate the fix and close this out with confidence.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference


From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@novabank.com>, NovaBank Engineering <eng+prod@novabank.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transparent incident debrief and verification instructions

Karthik —

I reviewed the attachments and added one small appendix in the Drive doc that enumerates the hash prefixes of affected model binaries (so their security team can confirm checksums). Also flagged the synthetic prompts we’ll share for the verification window.

Notes for the verification session:
- We should provide a short test harness (curl + token) so they can reproduce with minimal setup.
- Ask them to collect request_id headers for any failed runs and share as redacted logs.

Irene, can you confirm we’ve redacted any sensitive customer payloads from the timeline CSV?

-Marissa
Director, Customer Engineering
Redwood Inference

Cc: NovaBank Engineering <eng+prod@novabank.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transparent incident debrief and verification instructions

Thanks Karthik and team — this is very thorough and appreciated. A few points from our side after an initial read: 

- We do want the joint verification; 2027-04-25 works for us. I’ll loop in our security lead (cc’d: aisha@novabank.com).
- For the verification run, we’d like a short runbook: exact curl commands, expected HTTP codes, and a checklist for what to capture (request_id, duration, raw response body up to 1KB).
- Can you confirm whether any tenant-level data was persisted in a transient cache outside of our dedicated pool? Our compliance team asks specifically about cross-tenant leakage risk.

A few items we’ll bring on our side: a redacted sample of one failed request (we’ll anonymize identifiers) and a short list of production prompt shapes we use in peak hours.

Regards,
Sanjay Patel
SRE Lead, NovaBank

On Mon, Apr 19, 2027 at 11:02 AM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (appended notes + Drive link)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@novabank.com>, NovaBank Engineering <eng+prod@novabank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transparent incident debrief and verification instructions

Sanjay — thanks for the quick confirmation and for lining up the compliance contact. Answers inline below and next steps: 

- Runbook: attached a one-page validation-runbook in the Drive link ("validation-runbook.md") with exact curl examples, headers to include, and the expected pass/fail criteria. We’ll send a preconfigured token scoped to the joint verification for the 48-hour window.

- Cache persistence / cross-tenant risk: we validated that no tenant payloads were written to any shared long-term store. The transient KV-cache resides on the serving shard and is cleared on eviction; we audited traces and found no evidence of cross-tenant reads. We included checksums and verifier instructions in the Drive appendix so your security team can reproduce.

- Evidence we’re providing live during the window:
  * Per-request tracer showing request_id, shard, kernel-path, and eviction-event flag.
  * Synthetic prompts and expected token traces.
  * A watchlist of metrics we’ll monitor together (error-rate, p95/p99 latency, eviction-rate).

Next steps:
1) We will provision the verification token and share by EOD 2027-04-22.
2) Proposed window confirmed: 2027-04-25 00:00 UTC — 2027-04-26 23:59 UTC. Please confirm specific 2-hour overlap windows you'd like Redwood on-call and SRE present.
3) After the window, we’ll provide a short verification report and recommended guardrail configs.

If you prefer, we can also schedule a 30-minute pre-check run on 2027-04-23 to validate the harness.

Thanks — we want this closed with independent verification and minimal burden on your ops team.

-Karthik
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
